# pipixia frozen PHP product oracle

The reviewed `inputs.json` contains 49 synthetic metadata scenarios. It is not a production response fixture and it is not generated by Go.

`produce-pipixia.py` archives unchanged PHP commit `25beaee107f8c1a208ced9deb3c637068445e316` (tree `e4b9d40f5e6c12a86fff629c105553886b434dcd`) and requires PHP 8.3.6. The original platform functions execute against a strict cURL response tape, then the original entry JSON flags (320), adapter and public policy produce `php-baseline.json`. The manifest records the inputs, producers, immutable PHP source hashes, fixed clock and response digest. Unknown, reordered or unused requests fail generation.

The Go baseline tests use only that input tape and compare parser output, entry wire, request sequence, normal/debug public response, stable identities and defaults against the fixed PHP output. Successful tests export actual Go views through `DOKITOOL_GO_PIPIXIA_OUTPUT`; they never write expectations. `internal/api/pipixia_http_test.go` also exercises the actual catalog and HTTP handler for every fixture and resolves each successful item plus an absent target.

The controlled executor still checks purpose, URL authorization, metadata byte limit, method, headers, body, redirect handling and deadlines. This proves offline contract behavior, not current platform accessibility or a real browser/file save.

The 20-second business budget uses fixed microtime ticks and PHP ceiling semantics; real Go cancellation uses a genuine 20-second context. Entry flags do not apply JSON_NUMERIC_CHECK. Three invalid initial URLs have separate PHP gateway preflight expectations because the gateway rejects them before the platform parser.
